included: accepted state, effect, and receipt construction
Python, Rust, Tau, Lean, and proof-kernel refinement relations
atomic persistence and idempotent effect delivery required by accepted transitions
excluded: oracle truth and external market correctness
cryptographic primitive soundness below the declared library boundary
compiler, operating-system, hardware, and theorem-checker defects outside the declared TCB
user-interface correctness except where UI bytes become authority-bearing protocol input
economic optimality claims not stated as obligations in this profile

normative_transition.signature: Step(State, Command, Context) -> Reject(Error) | Accept(State, Effects, Receipt)
normative_transition.accepted: An accepted result contains one immutable successor state, one immutable effect plan, and one immutable receipt derived from the same pre-state, command, context, and candidate transition.
normative_transition.rejected: A rejected result contains no candidate state, no effects, no receipt, and authorizes no external mutation.
normative_transition.determinism: For canonical equal State, Command, and Context values, every conforming implementation returns byte-identical acceptance, error, successor state, effects, receipt, and roots.

obligations.title: Committed state transitively owns immutable values
obligations.statement: No caller-owned alias, mutable child, or behavior-changing subclass can alter or reinterpret committed state after construction.
blockers: Merge exact-head evidence for STATE-ALIAS-001, 002, 003, 004, and 007.
Re-run the complete state inventory at the release commit.

obligations.title: Authenticated intents own immutable meaning
obligations.statement: Authentication, hashing, nonce admission, settlement, and execution consume one recursively immutable intent value.
blockers: Merge authenticated-intent snapshot ownership.
Inventory every authenticated message type, including non-DEX modules.

obligations.title: Accepted effects and receipts own immutable values
obligations.statement: An accepted effect or receipt cannot change through a retained proposal, nested collection, event payload, or subclass after acceptance.
blockers: Merge accepted-effect and receipt snapshot ownership.
Inventory every effect and receipt type emitted by the system.

obligations.title: Accepted authority bytes have one semantic spelling
obligations.statement: The accepted bytes-to-value relation is injective for every command, state, proof context, effect, receipt, and persistence record.
blockers: Merge strict canonical JSON and fixed-hex boundaries.
Mount equivalent strict decoding at every remaining authority ingress.
Prove cross-language codec parity.

obligations.title: The normative transition is total over canonical inputs
obligations.statement: Every canonical State, Command, and Context tuple returns one explicit accepted or rejected result without process escape, undefined behavior, or unclassified exception.
blockers: Define the complete canonical state, command, and context domains.
Prove or exhaustively cover every constructor and transition branch.
Eliminate broad exception swallowing from authority paths.

obligations.title: Canonical equal inputs produce byte-identical results
obligations.statement: All conforming implementations return identical acceptance, rejection, state, effects, receipts, roots, and error codes for equal canonical inputs.
blockers: Complete deterministic time, ordering, arithmetic-width, and tie-break policies.
Run exhaustive differential replay across every promoted implementation.

obligations.title: Rejected transitions authorize no state or effects
obligations.statement: Every rejection carries only a canonical error and leaves pre-state, balances, nonces, effects, receipts, and outbox unchanged.
blockers: Add no-state/no-effect assertions to every command and failure family.
Prove shell rollback and crash recovery preserve the same relation.

obligations.title: Accepted transitions preserve all hard invariants
obligations.statement: For every accepted transition, all representation, conservation, authority, range, and lifecycle invariants hold in the successor state and effect plan.
blockers: Create a complete invariant inventory and map every invariant to source, proof, and regression evidence.
Separate representability invariants from derived health and policy conditions on every module.

obligations.title: All arithmetic is range-safe and rounding-explicit
obligations.statement: Every authoritative operation uses committed widths, checked domains, explicit rounding direction, and equivalent overflow behavior across implementations.
blockers: Complete integer-width and safe-range inventories.
Prove or exhaustively test every boundary, product, division, and cumulative accumulator.

obligations.title: Execution context is committed and replay-bound
obligations.statement: Chain, policy, time, oracle, validator, proof, algorithm, and configuration facts affecting acceptance are committed in State, Command, or Context and bound into roots and receipts.
blockers: Remove remaining host or environment authority from value-moving transitions.
Bind the same execution-context hash through final headers, proofs, effects, and receipts.

obligations.title: Every authoritative transition has a normative formal specification
obligations.statement: Each command, field, invariant, error, and effect is represented in a versioned formal specification whose semantics are the release authority.
blockers: Build a source-extracted command, field, invariant, effect, and error inventory.
Map every inventory item to Tau, Lean, Kani, proof-kernel, or explicitly justified executable-spec evidence.

obligations.title: Every executable implementation refines the same specification
obligations.statement: Python, Rust, Tau adapters, proof guests, and accelerated paths are proven or differentially demonstrated equivalent to the normative transition relation.
blockers: Complete Python-to-Rust and host-to-guest refinement for every promoted command.
Reject release when any shadow or production path lacks exact-SHA equivalence evidence.

obligations.title: Parallel execution is observationally equal to sequential execution
obligations.statement: Parallel computation may produce immutable facts or candidates only when final state, effects, rejection, roots, and receipts equal the normative sequential transition.
blockers: Freeze deterministic partitioning, reduction trees, ordering, and algorithm versions.
Prove or differentially test equality for every parallelized surface.

obligations.title: Command, field, error, effect, and invariant coverage is complete
obligations.statement: The release evidence inventory is generated from authoritative source and contains every reachable command, field, error, effect, invariant, and lifecycle terminal state.
blockers: Generate inventories from source rather than handwritten lists.
Fail closed on missing, duplicated, renamed, or untested inventory entries.

obligations.title: Boundary values and adversarial sequences cover the complete domain
obligations.statement: Every numeric boundary, lifecycle transition, replay path, alias path, malformed encoding, and adversarial command sequence is covered by reproducible tests or proofs.
blockers: Complete BVA matrices for every command and field.
Add stateful sequence, metamorphic, differential, and disaster-state campaigns with permanent minimized regressions.

obligations.title: State, effects, receipt, and outbox commit atomically
obligations.statement: The shell commits the accepted successor state, effect plan, receipt, nonce changes, and delivery identities in one expected-root transaction or commits none of them.
blockers: Define and implement one atomic persistence contract.
Prove crash points cannot expose partial accepted effects.

obligations.title: External effect delivery is exactly-once in semantic effect
obligations.statement: Every effect has a deterministic identity and retry protocol so crashes, duplicates, reordering, and replay cannot apply economic effects more than once.
blockers: Implement a transactional outbox keyed by accepted receipt and effect identity.
Add crash-recovery and duplicate-delivery proofs or exhaustive fault-injection tests.

obligations.title: Every release claim is bound to exact executed evidence
obligations.statement: Evidence identifies the exact source tree, toolchain, configuration, inputs, commands, outputs, and artifact hashes and is rejected when stale or unexecuted.
blockers: Unify audit, proof, test, differential, and release evidence under one signed manifest.
